A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references for comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: Section VII reports results obtained by implementing cited models, marked with stars in Table XII. These include CIFAR-100 classification and Cityscapes segmentation results, alongside results copied from prior publications.

after.justification: Section 7 explicitly attributes starred vision results to 'our own implementations.' Tables 12–15 report these results alongside published results across four vision datasets.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new distillation algorithm or model. Added descriptions of other researchers' methods expand the survey without changing a procedure proposed by this work.

E1.justification: Section 7 adds ImageNet classification and PASCAL VOC segmentation comparisons, including implementation-derived results in Tables 13–14. This substantially broadens the vision evaluation beyond CIFAR-100 and Cityscapes; the LLM benchmark coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The retained CIFAR-100 comparison adds CRD, OFD, InDistill, IKD, ADG-KD, and TeKAP as quantitatively compared methods (v1 Table XII versus v2 Table 12). The new ImageNet comparison also includes CAT-KD, NKD, and MLLD. These expand the actual comparison set, beyond additional citations.

E3.justification: Section 7 systematically expands comparisons to similar- and different-architecture teacher–student pairs, including ResNet32×4 to ShuffleNetV2 on CIFAR-100. Some Cityscapes settings are replaced: SKD's ResNet-101/MobileNetV2 entry becomes PSPNet-R101/PSPNet-R18 and PSPNet-R101/DeepLab-R18 entries. These are configuration changes, not evidence of same-setting performance improvements.

E4.justification: The expanded architecture pairs provide a limited architecture-sensitivity comparison, explicitly interpreted as evidence about architectural robustness in Section 8.3. This supplements v1's discussion of architectural differences, although no dedicated component ablations or controlled perturbation tests are added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seed lists, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the comparison tables. Parenthetical positive and negative numbers remain performance differences from baseline, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive ImageNet, PASCAL VOC, additional-method, and additional-architecture results. Some Cityscapes entries are replaced: SKD's 71.40 with MobileNetV2 becomes 74.23 with PSPNet-R18, under different reported settings. Existing CIFAR-100 rows and the LLM comparison retain their scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), covering logit, feature, similarity, adversarial, and contrastive distillation losses, retain their mathematical content. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about comprehensive coverage, the taxonomy, adaptive and contrastive distillation, 3D inputs, and modern foundation models. Expanded supporting material does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Sections 8.1–8.4 add classification principles, task-specific strategy recommendations, explicit qualifications against ranking heterogeneous results, and practical and ethical considerations. Table 17 provides selection guidance, while Section 8.4 qualifies privacy benefits with leakage and vulnerability concerns and discusses fairness, energy use, and copyright.

D1.justification: v2 supplies additional code hyperlinks, including for CRD, OFD, InDistill, and TeKAP. Retained segmentation entries also identify DeepLab or PSPNet architectures more precisely than v1's backbone-only names. Detailed training recipes, hardware specifications, and implementation budgets remain undisclosed.

R1.justification: The review adds recent methods and literature on industrial LLM distillation, including Gemma 3 and Qwen3, and on privacy and ethical concerns. These update coverage within the retained taxonomy; the positioning against earlier surveys remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local explanations are added, and the combined conclusion/discussion becomes an expanded Discussion followed by a separate Conclusion. Citation style, section numbering, and author presentation also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation with extensively reflowed figures and tables. The combined vision-results table becomes four dataset-specific tables with multiple architecture rows, and Table 17 adds practical guidance. Segmentation table headings change from 'mIoU' to 'Accuracy,' making their labeling less precise.

improvement.justification: The expanded vision comparisons and Section 8's practical guidance and qualifications make the survey more useful. These gains are tempered by new table defects: Table 13 prints TTM's ImageNet accuracy as 773.09, and the segmentation tables use 'Accuracy' where v1 specified mIoU. The central scientific account remains largely unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
